#### 5. schneckenbecken dysplasia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.379)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-727802)

**Proposed mechanism:** Solute carrier family 35 member A2 (HGNC:10692) —DISRUPTS→ UDP-GlcNAc transporter activity; UDP-GlcNAc transporter activity —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein biosynthesis (GO:0007275); Glycoprotein biosynthesis (GO:0007275) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); Solute carrier family 35 member D1 (HGNC:27116) —DISRUPTS→ Proteoglycan synthesis (GO:0007276); Proteoglycan synthesis (GO:0007276) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924); Glycoprotein biosynthesis (GO:0007275) —LEADS_TO→ Proteoglycan synthesis (GO:0007276). Mutations in SLC35A2 impair UDP-GlcNAc transport, disrupting glycoprotein biosynthesis and leading to developmental delay. Mutations in SLC35D1 impair proteoglycan synthesis, contributing to skeletal abnormalities. Both glycoprotein and proteoglycan synthesis are essential downstream processes of core glycosylation and are fundamentally linked, thus converging the disease modules.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if genetic analysis of Schneckenbecken dysplasia patients revealed no pathogenic variants in SLC35D1 or other genes involved in proteoglycan synthesis, and conversely, if SLC35A2 variants were found to be common in the general population (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 0.1%).

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact on glycosylation pathways, despite distinct genetic origins, could reveal novel therapeutic targets for improving protein and proteoglycan function in both congenital disorders of glycosylation and skeletal dysplasias.
